name: Risk Log
one_liner: Every identified risk in Cause-Risk-Effect form, scored L x I, with an owner and a response strategy.
purpose: The Risk Log is the central repository for all risks identified by the project, holding for each risk its likelihood, impact, risk level, response strategy and risk owner. It is used to document and communicate risks and the agreed risk-response actions and responsibilities, and is revised on the reassessment cycle fixed by the Risk Management Plan. Medium-to-high level risks are dealt with at a higher priority and reported regularly to the Project Steering Committee (PSC).
created_in: Initiating Phase (set up with the Issue and Decision Logs, p.31)
approved_by: n/a - maintained by the Project Manager (PM); for Manage Risk the PM is Responsible and the Project Owner (PO) Accountable (p.78)

lifecycle.what: Log set up; first risks taken from the Business Case
Risk Management Plan tailors scales, log structure and escalation thresholds
New risks added at any point; owners implement response actions
Reassessed on the agreed cycle; critical risks escalated to the PSC
Residual risks handed over; log feeds the Project-End Report

fields.what: The risk identifier. The template ships rows pre-numbered RL01-RL07; projects normally tailor the scheme in the Risk Management Plan.
Area affected by the risk: business, IT, people & organisation, external or legal; the template suggests Business, Staffing, Contractor, Legal.
fields.who: PM, from the categories set in the Risk Management Plan

fields.what: A short title for the risk, readable in a status report line.
fields.castor: Loss of Levallois's lead platform architect

fields.what: Structured Cause-Risk-Effect wording: 'Because of (CONDITION), it might be that (EVENT), which will lead to (IMPACT)', plus risk inter-dependencies.
fields.who: Identifier drafts; PM edits into Cause-Risk-Effect form
fields.castor: Because Levallois's design authority rests on a single architect, that architect might leave, delaying Release 2 (17/12/27).

fields.what: One of: Proposed, Assessing, Awaiting for Approval, Approved, Rejected, Closed. The guide prints 'Waiting for Approval'; the glossary prints 'investigating' for 'Assessing'.
fields.castor: Approved - accepted as a live risk on 16/10/26

fields.what: The name of the person who identified the risk. Anyone may identify a risk, at any point in the project.
The date on which the risk was identified, dd/mm/yy.
fields.castor: 25/09/26, one week after contract award to Levallois Systems

fields.what: Numerical estimate of the probability that the risk occurs: 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low.
fields.who: PM with the risk owner, at each reassessment

fields.what: Numerical value for the severity of the risk's impact should it occur: 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low.
fields.castor: 5 - Release 2 and the go-live date would slip

fields.what: The product of the two previous columns: RL = L * I. Values run 1-25 and set the priority and escalation band.
fields.castor: 20 (4 x 5) - top risk in the 31/03/27 Project Status Report

fields.what: The person accountable for managing and monitoring the risk. Need not be the PM, and is often outside the Managing Layer.
fields.who: PM proposes; PSC endorses for escalated risks
fields.castor: Leonardo da Vinci (SP), Head of IT & Digital Division

fields.what: Should the risk be escalated to the Directing or Steering Layers? Yes or No, per the thresholds in the Risk Management Plan.
fields.who: PM decides against the agreed threshold
fields.castor: Yes - RL 20 reported to the PSC on 31/03/27

fields.what: Threats: Avoid, Reduce, Accept, Transfer/Share. Opportunities: Exploit, Enhance, Accept, Share. The template lists only the four threat strategies.
The response action's objective, scope, deliverables, person responsible and estimated effort. Actions needing significant effort also go in the Project Work Plan.
fields.who: Risk owner defines; action responsible executes
fields.castor: Key-person clause plus 3-week knowledge transfer; Nikola Tesla co-designs; 15 PD.

fields.what: The date on which the risk response is expected to be implemented, dd/mm/yy.
IDs of the Project Work Plan tasks implementing the response, plus IDs of related changes, issues or decisions, and any comments.
fields.castor: PWP task 4.7; materialised 14/04/27 and re-raised as Issue I-11

traps: RL = L x I, a product; never L + I and never an average.
Appendix B prints status 'Assessing'; the glossary prints 'investigating' - same step.
Risk may happen; issue already happened; change alters the baseline. R-07 became I-11.
Risk Management Plan defines the process; the Risk Log holds the risks.
Exploit, Enhance, Share are opportunity strategies; Avoid, Reduce, Transfer are threats.
